recipes.name: Ladybug's Poppy Seed Chicken Casserole
ingredients_raw: 8 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, cooked and cut into bite-sized pieces
2 (10.75 ounce) cans condensed cream of chicken soup

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Mix together the cracker crumbs, melted butter, and poppy seeds in a bowl. Layer the bottom of a 9x13-inch glass baking dish with 2/3 of the cracker mix. Mix the chicken breast pieces with cream of chicken soup and sour cream until thoroughly combined, and spoon the mixture on top of the crumb crust. Sprinkle remaining 1/3 of the cracker mix over the top of the chicken mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven until the casserole is hot and bubbling, about 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Ladybug's Poppy Seed Chicken Casserole
raw_recipe.description: Creamy and comforting, this poppy seed chicken is easy to make and needs just a few ingredients.

review.reviewBody: My husband and I really liked this. The crumb mixture added a really nice touch. I didn't have poppy seeds and can't get them where I live, so I used sesame seeds instead. Next time I will shred the chicken instead of cutting it up into chunks, only because I didn't lcare for the chewy texture of the chunks of chicken in the casserole. It only took about 40 minutes to be hot and bubbly in my oven.
Delicious! I made this with light sour cream and light cream of chicken soup and you couldn't even tell! Our family devoured this--definitely will make again and again.

I've tried this several times by the recipe and it's always great. This time, I cut the recipe in half, added 2/3 cup of cooked rice and chopped up a small box of frozen broccoli. It was fantastic and no need to prepare sides!

My best friend's mother-in-law cooks a dish like this every time they visit her. She loved it but didn't have the exact measurements. We plugged in the ingredients on AR and this recipe showed up. We had a big group over last night so we doubled the butter, ritz crackers and chicken that the recipe calls for. Very different from anything I've ever tried but everyone cleaned their plates last night. Wonderful flavor. Next time I'll add some salt, pepper and maybe cheese.

Wow! This is soooo good! The only things I changed was I used 1/2 C butter instead of 1 cup and 3 chicken breasts instead of 8. The Ritz crackers are a yummy salty little crunch on the top! Thanks for sharing Ladybug!

I scaled the recipe in half, and reduced the butter by 50%, as well. I'm not convinced that much butter is necessary, and that amount negatively affects the nutritional breakdown. This recipe has no seasoning in it, and I was concerned that I’d end up with a casserole where all you could taste was sour cream and cream of chicken soup. I had odds and ends of veggies in the fridge, so I added a little chopped red onion, pimento, and bell pepper, in addition to a good shake of Trader Joe’s Mushroom and Company Umami Seasoning Blend and some freshly-ground black pepper. I’m just about burned out with tasteless, chewy chicken breasts, so I used poached boneless, skinless chicken thighs, a choice I’d make again. I know, I did make a few changes, but in the end, this turned out to be a really tasty chicken casserole. Garnished with some chopped parsley for a little eye appeal. We enjoy casseroles, and with my tweaks, I’ll make this again.

This really good! I've made several versions of poppy seed chicken and this filling is really good. I love that I don't have to cook it beforehand like some recipes. I prefer the cracker mixture on top also. Very good! I added some mozzarella cheese.

I made this today, but cut the recipe in half. I did sautee 8 oz. of sliced mushrooms and as suggested by another reviewer, added that along with 1 Tablespoon of sherry, too. I used one rotisserie chicken instead. Loved it! I will definitely make this again! Thanks so much for sharing.

I love this recipe and have made it many times over the years. I couldn't find my recipe and found this one on All Recipes today.
The only variations from this recipe and my original is that I add 8 oz. sliced mushrooms that have been sautéed lightly in butter. 
I also add 1-2 tablespoons of dry sherry.
This is an old Marshall Fields recipe from days gone by. Love it and thanks for sharing this one.

This was amazing! The only change I made was to add a can of Ortega chilies and serve over rice. I also used half a package of Costco's rotisserie chicken instead of cooking the breasts. My husband is still raving about this!
I have this recipe and thought I'd tell you that I added noodles to this and it becomes a hearty meal & I also use canned chicken.
Only change added broccoli. I didn't have two cans of cream of chicken so I used chicken broth and chicken Better than bouillon.
This recipe was very good but between the ritz, butter and soup was way too salty
I would put this over egg noodles next time.
It is always good! I've made it a few times. I had to omit the sour cream this time but it was still delicious.

This was very good. I made half a recipe. Added onions and a few carrots cause I needed to use them up. Maybe too much sauce without mashed potatoes to top. Need to Pam the bottom of the dish before putting the crumbs down. Mine stuck a little.
My daughter LOVES this recipe! She asks for it all the time! Definitely a family favorite!! Thank you for sharing!!
Tasted good, little too saucy, too buttery. Amounts need to be adjusted for better balance.
